text: At the surface it's bright, warm, and full of life. But sunlight fades fast in water.
By two hundred metres, it's like dusk. Most of the colours are gone. Red disappears first, then yellow, then green... until only a deep blue is left.
By one thousand metres, the sunlight is gone. Completely. From here to the bottom, it's the darkest place you can imagine. Darker than any night on land.
[whispering] Can somebody switch on a light?
Someone already has. Down here, animals make their own light. It's called bioluminescence.

Jellyfish flash blue when they're touched. Some shrimp spit glowing clouds to escape. And the anglerfish carries a little glowing lure on its head, like a fishing rod... and waits for something curious to swim close.
[cheerful, from the dark] Ooh. Nice light. Very friendly-looking.
[panicking] Don't go towards the light! Never go towards the light!
And we're only one kilometre down. The trench goes ten more.
